simple.meaning: אַיֵּה (ʼayêh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “where?.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 47 times across Genesis, Exodus, Judges, 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, and 11 more, beginning at Genesis 18:9. Its contexts include family, family line, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַיֵּה (H346).

definitions.full: H346. ayyeh אַיֵּה 45 (lengthened from אַי , compare הֵן & הִנֵּה ) interr.adverb Where? Gen 18:9 ; 19:5 ; 22:7 ; the most General term expressing this idea, used of both person & things (but never with a verb [contrast אֵיפֹה ]); often in poetry or elevated style, where the answer nowhere is expected, Isa 33:18 ; 36:19 ; 51:13 ; Jer 2:28 (compare Deut 32:37 אֵי ) Jer 17:15 ; 37:19 , Job 15:23 he wandereth abroad for bread אַיֵּה (saying) Where is it ? 21:28 ; Zech 1:5 ( אַיֵּההֵֿם ); in the (iron.) phrase where is thy ( their ) God ? Psa 42:4 ; 42:11 ; 79:10 ; 115:2 ( אַיֵּהנָֿא ) Joel 2:17 ; rhetorically, of an earnest inquiry Jer 2:6 , 8 ; Job 35:10 , or longing Isa 63:11 , 15 ; Judg 6:13 .
